svg.title: Design Subscription Economics in Context
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-design-subscription-benchmarks; chapter number: 2; title: Design Subscription Economics in Context; subtitle: Distinguish operating costs, launch pricing, package pricing, and a teaching target.; caption: Brett Williams reports Designjoy's tool cost and package price; Harry Roper reports their launch price. Starter Story also presents a $500-versus-$5,000 client contrast.; assumptions note: Brett Williams's $25,000 monthly figure is a teaching target, not a promised result. Harry Roper's launch price is a separate business example. Each equal minimum, maximum, and typical value represents a quoted point, not a measured distribution. The $500 client contrast has no stated billing cadence.; note: Brett Williams on Starter Story — dXKzST0FE-A at 00:04:54; Creative Crew with Brad Hussey — o-UR3rkPgJ4 at 00:01:36; The Futur — 8vwgUwgH2Js at 00:43:19; Harry Roper — rO0i7sGwhCU at 00:00:00; Starter Story — vedkm3ZmHIE at 00:05:33. Williams separately identifies payment fees and taxes.; chart type: horizontal_bars; unit: USD; billing cadence and economic meaning shown per bar; bars: label: Williams operating tools; min: 176; max: 176; typical: 176; display: $176/month reported tool cost; label: Starter Story lower-price client; min: 500; max: 500; typical: 500; display: $500 client contrast; cadence unstated; label: Roper launch subscription; min: 1000; max: 1000; typical: 1000; display: $1,000/month launch price; label: Williams popular subscription; min: 5000; max: 5000; typical: 5000; display: $5,000/month package; label: Williams teaching target; min: 25000; max: 25000; typical: 25000; display: Five clients at $5,000 = $25,000/month
